findings.body: The request is rejected because both predicates must be true, so team admins cannot use the feature despite isTeamAdmin accepting either ADMIN or OWNER.
findings.failure_mode: Valid team-admin requests are incorrectly returned as FORBIDDEN.
findings.impact: The request is rejected because both predicates must be true, so team admins cannot use the feature despite isTeamAdmin accepting either ADMIN or OWNER.
findings.root_cause: The authorization expression requires membership to satisfy both the admin-or-owner role check and the owner-only role check.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the team-admin predicate alone, or combine the intended admin and owner checks with the appropriate OR logic instead of requiring both.
findings.title: Team admins who are not owners are denied access
findings.trigger: A team member with the ADMIN role but without the OWNER role invokes addGuests for a booking belonging to that team.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 47-48 shows `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The isTeamAdmin function (L264-284) accepts ADMIN or OWNER roles, but isTeamOwner (L286-295) only accepts OWNER. Using && means both must be true, so ADMIN-only users fail the isTeamAdminOrOwner check despite the variable name suggesting otherwise.

findings.body: The handler passes both entries to createMany, creating duplicate attendee records and causing duplicate calendar and email processing.
findings.failure_mode: Direct API callers can create duplicate booking attendees even though the UI rejects exact duplicates.
findings.impact: The handler passes both entries to createMany, creating duplicate attendee records and causing duplicate calendar and email processing.
findings.root_cause: Server-side validation only checks email syntax and leaves duplicate elimination to a client-side refinement.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce uniqueness in the server schema or normalize and deduplicate the guest list in the handler before createMany.
findings.title: The API accepts duplicate guest addresses in one request
findings.trigger: A caller sends a valid tRPC request containing the same email more than once, such as guests: ["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"].
findings.verifier_reason: Line 5 shows `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. The client-side AddGuestsDialog.tsx L26-29 has a refine for uniqueness, but the server schema lacks it. Direct API calls can submit duplicates which pass to createMany at L101-103, creating duplicate attendee records.

findings.body: The case-variant address is treated as new and another attendee row is inserted for the same mailbox, leading to duplicate invitations and attendee data.
findings.failure_mode: Equivalent email identities bypass duplicate suppression.
findings.impact: The case-variant address is treated as new and another attendee row is inserted for the same mailbox, leading to duplicate invitations and attendee data.
findings.root_cause: Existing-attendee detection uses case-sensitive string equality for email addresses.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare normalized email addresses, for example by lowercasing both existing and incoming addresses, and deduplicate the normalized request list before insertion.
findings.title: Email comparisons allow case-variant duplicate attendees
findings.trigger: A booking already contains Guest@example.com and a caller adds guest@example.com, optionally alongside another new guest.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 76 shows `guest === attendee.email` using strict equality. Email addresses are case-insensitive per RFC, so 'Guest@example.com' would not match 'guest@example.com' in booking.attendees, allowing case-variant duplicates to be inserted.

findings.body: The blocked mailbox is inserted as an attendee and receives the booking invitation, bypassing the configured blacklist.
findings.failure_mode: Configured guest-email blocking is inconsistently enforced based on address casing.
findings.impact: The blocked mailbox is inserted as an attendee and receives the booking invitation, bypassing the configured blacklist.
findings.root_cause: Blacklist entries are lowercased but the submitted guest address is compared without normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the incoming guest address before comparison, or use a case-insensitive predicate against the normalized blacklist entries.
findings.title: Uppercase variants bypass the guest email blacklist
findings.trigger: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains blocked@example.com and an authorized user submits Blocked@example.com.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 71 lowercases blacklist entries but line 77 uses `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where guest is not lowercased. Submitting 'Blocked@example.com' when 'blocked@example.com' is blacklisted bypasses the check since includes() is case-sensitive.

raw_findings.body: The attendee rows are inserted, but EventManager is initialized with the actor's credentials and cannot update the organizer's existing external calendar event, leaving the calendar invite without the new guest or causing the mutation to fail after the database change.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Database state and external calendar state diverge for authorized non-organizer requests.
raw_findings.impact: The attendee rows are inserted, but EventManager is initialized with the actor's credentials and cannot update the organizer's existing external calendar event, leaving the calendar invite without the new guest or causing the mutation to fail after the database change.
raw_findings.root_cause: Calendar synchronization credentials are selected from the authenticated actor even though the endpoint explicitly permits non-organizers to modify the organizer's booking.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Load and pass the credentials associated with the booking's organizer or referenced calendar credentials when synchronizing the booking, while retaining the actor only for authorization.
raw_findings.title: Adding guests as an attendee can fail to update the organizer's calendar
raw_findings.trigger: An attendee or team administrator, rather than the booking organizer, adds a guest while the acting user has no credentials matching the booking's calendar references.

raw_findings.body: The constructed event has no team or team.members property, so sendAddGuestsEmails cannot enter its team-member loop and only the organizer receives the add-guest notification.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The intended team-recipient notification path is unreachable for this endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: The constructed event has no team or team.members property, so sendAddGuestsEmails cannot enter its team-member loop and only the organizer receives the add-guest notification.
raw_findings.root_cause: The handler constructs a new CalendarEvent without copying the team membership data required by the newly added notification path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Load the event's team members and populate the CalendarEvent team field, or pass the team members explicitly to the email manager.
raw_findings.title: Team members are never included in add-guest notifications
raw_findings.trigger: A booking for a team event is updated through this handler.
